findings.title: Unknown protection kinds silently select plaintext
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Fix before publishing the affected supported operation

reproduction.stepsAndObservedResult: kind=passpharse, unknown or undefined returned NoProtection and actual plaintext MNCL bytes (encrypted=false). Valid CLI choices were not shown to leak.
reproduction.fixture: Public BIP39/SSKR vectors or tiny synthetic data only

findings.expected: docs/CANDIDATES.md and NoProtection's declaration reserve plaintext for an explicit choice; a parsed/JavaScript protection discriminant must reject unsupported kinds instead of selecting another operation.
findings.observed: kind=passpharse, unknown or undefined returned NoProtection and actual plaintext MNCL bytes (encrypted=false). Valid CLI choices were not shown to leak.
findings.impact: A JavaScript or parsed host request must contain an invalid kind. Valid typed CLI choices are unaffected. No actual user list was written, no encryption failure or theft is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Handle choice.kind==='none' explicitly, reject all other kinds and malformed choice objects; keep the existing three implementation classes.

findings.title: Accepted non-minimal short CBOR is forwarded unchanged to a decoder that rejects it
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Fix before publishing the affected supported operation

reproduction.stepsAndObservedResult: The canonical public quorum restored correctly. Its accepted nonminimal short CBOR variant paired with the second member was refused by the real engine: These shares do not restore a secret. Existing repair tests explicitly call this layout supported.
reproduction.fixture: Public BIP39/SSKR vectors or tiny synthetic data only

findings.expected: The current repair regression explicitly calls non-minimal short CBOR length layouts supported. transport.sharePayload accepts 0x58 followed by a length below 24. Accepted shares should retain the same secret and be usable by the production restore.
findings.observed: The canonical public quorum restored correctly. Its accepted nonminimal short CBOR variant paired with the second member was refused by the real engine: These shares do not restore a secret. Existing repair tests explicitly call this layout supported.
findings.impact: Recovery/interoperability failure limited to already accepted non-minimal short heads; no evidence that canonical, normally generated shares fail. No cryptographic break or secret loss demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Locally re-encode the already validated payload with the shortest supported byte-string head in transportToUr and recompute CRC, then compare canonical URs. Keep support for legacy/current tags. This is a correctness fix, not reopening the deferred cross-language ownership task G1-001.
findings.requiredVerification: One tiny real-production restore for the non-minimal variant plus a canonical control; identical payload variants deduplicate where copy-removal is promised. No rebuild or full vector replay is proposed.

findings.title: A share mixing code-point and whole-color marks has no Color Unicode reading
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Fix before publishing the affected supported operation

reproduction.stepsAndObservedResult: A public third share with one code-point mark and one complete-color mark, alongside two intact quorum members, produced no-fit. The correct mixed width model is never enumerated. No large search ran.
reproduction.fixture: Public BIP39/SSKR vectors or tiny synthetic data only

findings.expected: docs/SSKR.md:130 permits replacing an unreadable Color Unicode code or pair with ?. repair.ts describes a mark standing for one code or a whole color. It states no requirement that every mark in a share use the same width.
findings.observed: A public third share with one code-point mark and one complete-color mark, alongside two intact quorum members, produced no-fit. The correct mixed width model is never enumerated. No large search ran.
findings.impact: Damaged Color Unicode input mixing the documented code/pair mark units. Homogeneous marks and other share forms are unaffected by this reasoning. This establishes an omitted reading, not a wrong restored wallet.
findings.recommendedFix: Enumerate compatible per-mark one/two-code widths with early parity, unit-count and layout pruning, under an explicit bound. Do not use an unbounded 2^marks expansion or silently discard valid readings when the bound is reached.
findings.requiredVerification: The tiny mixed-mark production case, its homogeneous controls, and a bounded refusal for highly ambiguous mark widths.

findings.title: CLI PDF saves use a replacing writer despite the no-overwrite contract
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Fix before publishing the affected supported operation

reproduction.stepsAndObservedResult: After real CLI path preflight, a synthetic file appeared at that path; the actual exportCards publication adapter replaced it (refused=false, preserved=false). Only rendering was stubbed with opaque public bytes; no PDF was generated.
reproduction.fixture: Public BIP39/SSKR vectors or tiny synthetic data only

findings.expected: Saving.write promises never to write over anything at the destination. README.md:307 promises existing files/folders are preserved; preflight picks a free numbered name. That promise must still hold if the chosen name appears after preflight.
findings.observed: After real CLI path preflight, a synthetic file appeared at that path; the actual exportCards publication adapter replaced it (refused=false, preserved=false). Only rendering was stubbed with opaque public bytes; no PDF was generated.

Rendering was stubbed; no actual PDF, wallet backup loss or hostile-host exploit was demonstrated. Normally existing names are renumbered, so the failure needs a later collision.
findings.recommendedFix: Use exclusive private-file publication for CLI PDF saves, preserving the intentionally supported replacement API if existing callers rely on it. Route Encode and Preview through the same exclusive adapter and retain preflight name selection.

findings.title: Undefined or truthy nonboolean wallet answers can become date matches
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Fix before publishing the affected supported operation

reproduction.entry: mnemocode/core/date-search: DateSearch.run with a runtime JavaScript walletCheck
reproduction.stepsAndObservedResult: A configured callback returning undefined or {matched:'false'} yielded matchCount=1. Boolean false and true controls yielded 0 and 1. This is faulty-host return validation, not protection against a dishonest checker.
reproduction.fixture: Public BIP39/SSKR vectors or tiny synthetic data only

findings.expected: WalletCheck returns a WalletMatch with a boolean matched field. Listing every checksum-valid candidate is supported when no wallet callback is configured, not when a configured callback returns an invalid answer.
findings.observed: A configured callback returning undefined or {matched:'false'} yielded matchCount=1. Boolean false and true controls yielded 0 and 1. This is faulty-host return validation, not protection against a dishonest checker.
findings.impact: Requires a malformed JavaScript host service; built-in Node evidence checks return proper boolean objects. False recovery confidence is a plausible API impact, not an observed CLI compromise.
findings.recommendedFix: When a wallet callback exists, require a non-null object and boolean matched; accept only matched===true. Reject malformed callback results with a public contract error; keep the no-wallet listing path explicit.
findings.requiredVerification: Add the exact public reproduction and well-formed controls to the affected production-path tests; preserve messages and ownership

findings.title: Malformed UTF-8 from a file or stdin may silently change passphrase text
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Fix before publishing the affected supported operation

reproduction.stepsAndObservedResult: A tiny passphrase file ending in byte FF and LF was accepted with U+FFFD replacing FF. No KDF or wallet derivation was needed. Intentionally valid UTF-8 U+FFFD must remain allowed.
reproduction.fixture: Public BIP39/SSKR vectors or tiny synthetic data only

findings.expected: CLI help calls the BIP39 passphrase file the wallet's passphrase; candidate protection documents text as entered. Terminal answers use fatal UTF-8 decoding, and Bip39Seed rejects malformed Unicode strings before deriving.
findings.observed: A tiny passphrase file ending in byte FF and LF was accepted with U+FFFD replacing FF. No KDF or wallet derivation was needed. Intentionally valid UTF-8 U+FFFD must remain allowed.
findings.impact: Malformed or misencoded passphrase files are accepted as changed Unicode text. The probe established replacement decoding, not an actual wrong wallet or encryption run. Valid UTF-8 remains supported; a malformed file has no uniquely inferable intended Unicode password.

findings.title: Custom template capacity is not checked before calculating or iterating its cards
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Fix before publishing the affected supported operation

reproduction.stepsAndObservedResult: Otherwise complete stock-template objects with capacities -1, Infinity or NaN returned zero cards; 0 and 0.5 reached the rendering callback before refusal. reproduction.fixture: Public BIP39/SSKR vectors or tiny synthetic data only

findings.expected: CardTemplate explicitly permits designs made by a host. referencesPerCard means the positive whole number of references assigned to each separate card, and a returned collection must contain the input references rather than silently disappearing.
findings.observed: Otherwise complete stock-template objects with capacities -1, Infinity or NaN returned zero cards; 0 and 0.5 reached the rendering callback before refusal. A sentinel stopped immediately before rendering. Capacity 1 was the valid control. No infinite loop or PDF was executed.

recommendations.what: New areWordIndexes predicate in bip39-sizes.ts, now the only dense check of a word-index list; assertWordIndexes calls it. progressStep keeps its undefined branch and otherwise calls keptCount(every, 1, 'progressEvery', 1); the RangeError message is the same. New wholeNumbersFrom(min) in typed-number.ts; keptCount uses it. WordCandidate checks its number with inWholeRange(number, CANDIDATE_NUMBERS) and keeps its own RangeError text.
CASHADDR_160_GROUPS is now bech32Groups(1 + HASH160_BYTES) + CASHADDR_CHECKSUM_GROUPS. The local GROUP_BITS and the literal 8 are removed.

bip39-sizes.ts now has lastWordEntropyValues(wordCount) = 2^lastWordEntropyBits and checksumPassShare(wordCount) = 2^-checksumBits. The private checks and lastShift callbacks of Masking now take the word count and use these functions. The Seedshift tail modulus (seedshift.ts), the loop in validLastWordIndexes (words.ts) and expectedCandidates (candidates.ts) use them too. Powers of two keep every value exact; a test pins the table for every mode and length.

There is now one pure linearize(map, origin, directions) and a unitVectors(count) helper. Both are exported from src/sskr/repair.ts, not gf2.ts, because gf2.ts belongs to the shares group (a move is offered in needsOtherGroup). Evaluation order is the same (origin first, then each direction in order). residualAt still wipes its payload locally, and each caller still supplies its own directions. Afterwards linearize and unitVectors moved to src/sskr/gf2.ts, their linear-algebra owner.

There is now one non-owning xorInto(target, delta), exported from src/sskr/repair.ts, not core/bits.ts, because bits.ts belongs to the core group (a move is offered in needsOtherGroup). It replaces three copies: joint-repair's private xorInto, the per-byte loop in ReadingSpace.payloadAt, and the two `other.map(byte ^ base[index])` copies. In ReadingSpace.solve and splitByDigest.deltaOf, the freshly made payload or (S, D) array now becomes the delta in place. Before, the code made a copy and wiped the original. Afterwards xorInto moved to src/core/bits.ts, imported by both repair modules.
